div.p: The conventional task models include periodic tasks, aperiodic tasks and sporadic tasks. A task model named rhythmic task is required for Cyber Physical Systems (CPS). Here, a Smart Energy Management System (SEMS) in a house, which monitors and controls the electrical appliances based on their power demand, has been considered as the CPS. The temperature control of air conditioner, which has high priority, is the rhythmic task. Sensing of temperature, pressure, etc, are periodic tasks. This paper deals with the schedulability test for a combined model of rhythmic and periodic tasks of SEMS. The test had been simulated and the given task set was found to be schedulable.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Conventional task models are periodic tasks [2] and aperiodic tasks [9]. But these task models are not enough for handling all types of tasks. Another type of task model is sporadic tasks [3]. Yet another one is rhythmic tasks [1]. In this paper, a schedulability test for rhythmic tasks has been explained in the context of smart energy management system, which is a Cyber-Physical System.

"A new generation of system that integrates computing and communication capabilities with the dynamics of physical and engineering based system is called as Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)" [5]. Examples for CPS are biomedical systems, automotive systems, smart energy management systems [13], etc. CPS must operate safely, securely, efficiently and in realtime while interacting with the physical world [4].

"A rhythmic task is defined as a task which has continuously varying time period and varying Worst Case Execution Time (WCET), depending on external physical events" [1]. In automotive system, fuel injection to each cylinder is considered as a rhythmic task [1]. In the case of the smart energy management system considered in this paper, the control action of Passive Infrared (PIR) sensor has been identified as a rhythmic task.

As the time period and WCET of the rhythmic tasks are continuously varying, hence the conventional Utilization Bound (UB) test [2] or Response Time Analysis (RTA) are not enough for determining the schedulability of these tasks. This is because these conventional methods do not have any provision for handling continuously varying time period and WCET. Hence, a schedulability test [1] for rhythmic tasks has been explained in this paper and the simulation result for the same has been provided, as a case study. This schedulability test can be included in the Real Time Operating System (RTOS) [9] which is used in the CPS, in order to determine the schedulability of the rhythmic task.

The scheduling test for one rhythmic and many periodic tasks, which had been developed for automotive systems [1] has been applied in this paper for smart energy management system. This papers aims to explore the applicability of rhythmic task schedulability test for SEMS.

The paper is organized as follows. Section II gives the background study. Section III explains the rhythmic task model and the schedulability test for scheduling one rhythmic task and many periodic tasks. A case study for rhythmic task model has been provided in Section IV. Simulation result is given in Section V and conclusion in Section VI.

div.head: II. BACKGROUND STUDY
div.p: In the history of real time systems, different task models have been studied in detail like the periodic tasks [2], aperiodic tasks [9], sporadic tasks [3], etc. A newly found task model is the rhythmic task model [1], which is of great importance in the context of CPS. CPS is a system which has both computing and communication capabilities, integrated with the physical system. In a CPS, for example in an automotive system, if fuel delivery does not take place at correct time, then, the results can be disastrous [1]. Yet in another CPS like a smart energy management system, if a task like the control action of a PIR sensor used, does not meet its deadline, then it can lead to reduction in efficiency of the smart energy management system. The latter has been dealt in detail as case study for rhythmic tasks in this paper. The conventional schedulability tests like the UB test [2] and RTA test are not enough for handling rhythmic tasks, as they do not have any provision for handling continuously varying time period and WCET. If these rhythmic tasks are not scheduled properly, then it can have disastrous results or reduction in efficiency of the system, depending on the CPS under consideration. Hence, it is important to have a good schedulability test for rhythmic tasks. A schedulability test for rhythmic tasks and its simulation result have been explained in this paper using the modified RTA test [1]. Some other task models which have been studied in the past are as follows: elastic task models for dynamic priority scheduling [6], gravitational task models for non-preemptive job scheduling [7], mode change protocol [8], etc. In elastic task model, tasks are considered as springs with elastic coefficients, to perform better under loaded conditions [6]. Usually, earlier start time and deadlines are preferred for tasks, for feasibility. But for some tasks, execution should take place at a particular target point for maximum utility. In gravitational task model, tasks are considered as massive bobs hanging from pendulum. A single task, left to itself, will execute at the bottom which is the target point. If weight of some other tasks comes, then it will be executed at some other point [7]. Both these models are used in multimedia, control applications, etc. In some real time applications, the characteristics of tasks might change while execution. Mode change can occur, i.e.., addition, deletion or changes in the parameters of tasks. Increasing sampling rate for better accuracy is an example for this. A protocol to accommodate these, in a priority-driven preemptive scheduling environment is known as mode change protocol [8].
In this paper, rhythmic task model is being discussed. The definitions and scheduling properties have been referred from reference [1].

div.head: III. THE RHYTHMIC TASK MODEL
div.p: A rhythmic task is defined as a task which has continuously varying time period and varying Worst Case Execution Time (WCET), depending on current physical attributes of the system. The rhythmic task model is mainly for cyber-physical requirements and gives better utilization. A state vector v s represents the physical attributes of the given system. A set of hard real-time tasks = { 1 , 2 , …, n } are considered here, where n represents the number of tasks. Given n tasks, out of which m are rhythmic tasks, then, (n-m) periodic tasks are there. A periodic task i is represented as (C i , T i , D i ), where C i is its WCET, T i is its time period, and D i is the deadline. A rhythmic task i * is specified as

). Here the WCET, time period, and deadline are functions of v s . Assumptions similar to Rate-Monotonic Scheduling (RMS) [2] are made here. It is assumed that T i = D i and T i * = D i * . In this paper, we are considering the case of one rhythmic task (m=1) and many periodic tasks only. The rhythmic task is assumed to have the highest priority always and hence the shortest time period. This is in accordance to the assumptions of RMS [1].

div.head: IV. A SCHEDULABILITY TEST FOR ONE RHYTHMIC TASK AND MANY PERIODIC TASKS
div.p: An algorithm has been developed to find whether one rhythmic task and many periodic tasks are schedulable or not. This schedulability test had been written using algorithm 1, algorithm 2, algorithm 3 and algorithm 4, in the context of an automotive system [1].

div.p: In the above algorithm, n α refers to the maximum acceleration duration of the rhythmic task. In step 3 of the algorithm, maximum possible computation time of the rhythmic task is calculated by using a function Rhythm_Max_C(C,T,n) (Algorithm 1 of [1]) where C is the WCET, T is the time period and n is the number of tasks. In step 6 of the algorithm, response time of periodic task is calculated by using modified equation for RTA test which considers number of preemptions and execution time, by using functions Num_Preemptions(T[0],alpha,n_alpha,W[k]) and Execution_Time(np,C[0],alpha,n_alpha) (Algorithm 3 and 4 of [1]), respectively. Here, W[k] is the response time, np is the number of preemptions, C[0] and T[0] are the WCET and time period of rhythmic task, respectively. In modified equation for RTA test, number of preemptions and execution time are considered in addition to the existing RTA test [14] [16].

div.head: V. CASE STUDY OF RHYTHMIC TASK MODEL
div.p: Here the CPS under consideration is a smart energy management system [12] [17] in a house.

The smart energy management system of the house, shown in Fig. 1, consists of three intelligent sensor nodes [12]. Each of these nodes consists of temperature sensor, pressure sensor, humidity sensor and passive infrared (PIR) sensor. The intelligent sensor nodes, depending on human presence and environmental conditions, make decisions regarding whether appliances are to be turned on/ off, automatically. To the three nodes critical, very critical and normal loads are connected. The parameters like temperature, humidity, luminance, energy demand, etc could be displayed in a Graphical User Interface (GUI), at the central server. This helps to monitor the energy consumption of the house from a different location. In case, if the generation of power is lesser than the demand, then the appliances can be turned off depending on their criticality. The turned off devices can be turned on, if required, once the generation of power is equal to the demand. For better energy management of the system, RTOS [10] is used here for scheduling the different periodic and rhythmic tasks. Hence, the smart energy meter in the house is also called as smart embedded module. The communication between smart embedded module and central server takes place through a gateway.

The controlling actions of PIR sensor, i,e., controlling the speed of fan, brightness of lamp and temperature control of air conditioner in the house, are identified as rhythmic tasks. These rhythmic tasks are affected by human presence, which is the external physical event in the system. For simulation purpose, one rhythmic task alone is considered here, which is temperature control of air conditioner. Some periodic tasks identified in this system are sensing of temperature, pressure, humidity and human presence by temperature sensor, pressure sensor, humidity sensor and PIR sensor, respectively. The time period of the rhythmic task varies in the range 20ms to 50ms. The periodic tasks are: 2 (5ms, 105ms), 3 (5ms, 110ms), 4 (5ms, 115ms) and 5 (5ms, 120ms). Task 1 is temperature control of air conditioner, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are sensing of temperature, pressure, humidity and human presence, by the intelligent sensor node, respectively. The schedulability test for one rhythmic task and multiple periodic tasks have been applied to this task set. The algorithm for the scheduling test has been developed in C. The simulation result obtained from Dev C++ Integrated Development Environment (IDE) is shown in Fig. 2.

div.head: VI. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
div.p: The scheduling test for one rhythmic and many periodic tasks, which had been developed for automotive systems [1] has been applied in this paper for smart energy management system. The scheduling test algorithm have been developed in C language and compiled in Dev C++ IDE. The simulation result for smart energy management system is given in Fig. 2. For the case study done, the task sets have been found to be schedulable. In the smart energy management system considered here, a total of five tasks have been considered. Task 1 is temperature control of air conditioner, which is the rhythmic task. It is the highest priority task. Task 2, task 3, task 4 and task 5 are sensing of temperature, pressure, humidity and human presence by the intelligent sensor node, respectively. These four are the periodic tasks considered for simulation. 20ms to 50ms has been given as the range of time period for rhythmic task. From the given range, 50ms has been randomly chosen as the time period of rhythmic task. For this time period, 30ms is calculated as the maximum possible computation time by the algorithm. Using this particular time period and WCET of rhythmic task, schedulability is checked along with other periodic tasks. The result is obtained as schedulable for the given task set. This paper deals with the simulation of schedulability test for one rhythmic task and many periodic tasks. The schedulability test, which was developed for an automotive system in reference [1], has been applied to a smart energy management system in this paper. The algorithm for this schedulability test was developed using C language and the simulation results have been obtained using Dev C++ IDE. In the given task set, for rhythmic task alone, a range is specified for time period. Depending on the randomly chosen time period (within the given range), the maximum possible computation time is calculated by the algorithm and then the schedulability of task set is checked. As future works, this schedulability test can be extended for many rhythmic tasks. This can be applied in different areas like biomedical, robotics, etc.
